title: Maintenance runbook: RFC intake, review checklist, and deprecation matrix for tokens & components
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Purpose:
This ticket captures a pragmatic, centralized runbook for ongoing maintenance of the design system: how new RFCs for tokens/components are accepted, the formal review checklist design/engineering must follow, and a risk-based deprecation matrix to retire visual tokens and components safely. The deliverable is a single canonical document (Confluence) plus a lightweight intake form and a templated RFC that Product/Design/Eng can use.

Scope:
- Tokens (color, spacing, typography scale)
- Core components (buttons, tables, form controls, charts primitives)
- Migration guidance and automated codemod triggers owned by ENG

Intake flow (high level):
1) Author fills RFC template (short problem statement + migration cost estimate + suggested compatibility strategy). Provide link to prototype/PR where relevant.
2) Submit intake form (links to RFC doc, target release, and risks). Triage board (weekly) assigns reviewer pair: designer + eng owner.
3) Review pass 1: checklist validation (see below). If checklist passes, RFC marked "Approved for implementation" with rollout constraints. If not, iterate.
4) Implementation: feature branch, tests, docs, and codemods if non-trivial token changes.
5) Rollout & monitor: canary release, telemetry for visual regressions, cadence for follow-up.
6) Deprecation: schedule per matrix (below).

Review checklist (must be addressed by submitter and reviewers):
- Problem clarity: why current tokens/components are insufficient?
- Backwards compatibility: can old tokens map to new ones? Strategy for aliasing?
- Migration cost: estimate (dev hours, UI audit scope).
- Automated support: codemod plan or library shim needed?
- RTL/accessibility: keyboard/ARIA implications tested.
- Performance: render/paint impact for component changes (tables/charts).
- Observability: dashboard metrics to track (errors, regressions, adoption).
- Docs & examples: playground + snippet for both new and legacy usage.
- Testing: unit + visual snapshot + integration tests where appropriate.
- Rollback plan: steps to revert change if regressions appear.

Deprecation matrix (risk-based):
- High risk (core tokens used across >40 apps / buttons & primary tokens): deprecation window = 26 weeks; requires canary + replacement alias + codemod; release approvals from eng lead + PM.
- Medium risk (specialized tokens / secondary components): deprecation window = 13 weeks; aliasing recommended; opt-in migration.
- Low risk (experimental tokens, non-platform charts): deprecation window = 6 weeks; announce and remove if no adoption.

Rollout recommendations:
- Always provide aliases for at least two releases (or 13 weeks) for tokens referenced in public API.
- Use feature flags for component behavior changes with gradual ramp.
- Inform downstream owners via an automated notice (Slack + email digest) and create a Linear ticket per impacted product team.

Owner responsibilities:
- Design: provide spec, visual QA checklist, accessibility review.
- Eng: implement codemods, add metrics, ensure performance goals.
- PM: prioritize migration windows and communicate SLAs to customers.

Deliverables:
- Confluence doc: canonical runbook + intake form link (DOC-DesignSystem-Maintenance).
- RFC template: rfc/component-token-template.md in repo.
- Intake form: short Google Form (or internal form) that creates a seeded Linear ticket.
- Example codemod PR and tests.

Success criteria:
- 90% of incoming token/component changes follow the intake & checklist within 8 weeks.
- No high-severity visual regressions roll out without a rollback in place.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We favor longer deprecation windows for tokens because cross-product migration cost is high. For low-use experimental components we will iterate faster to avoid accumulating technical debt.
- Codemods increase upfront cost but dramatically reduce long-term maintenance; require ENG commitment for automation.
